title: Unique identifier linking
description: The face authentication system may link data collected by the camera to individuals based on unique identifiers, thereby establishing a linkage between the data and the identity of the subjects captured by the camera.

title: Identifiable information processing
description: The camera captures facial images that can be processed to derive the identity of individuals, making it possible for the system to process identifiable information.

title: Sensitive data types collection
description: Facial images collected from the camera may be considered highly sensitive data types and could lead to data disclosure risks if not handled properly.

title: GDPR-related noncompliance
description: There may be GDPR-related noncompliance risks if the processing of personal data captured by the camera does not meet the requirements for lawful processing, including obtaining valid consent.

title: Identifiable information is processed
description: The face authentication system processes identifiable information, enabling the derivation of the identity of the data subject who is being authenticated.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: The face authentication system may collect biometric data which is considered highly sensitive and should only be processed when strictly necessary.

title: GDPR-related noncompliance
description: The face authentication system may violate GDPR principles by failing to implement necessary data subject controls and consent mechanisms required for processing biometric data.

title: Unique identifier: Linking based on unique identifier
description: The face authentication system uses unique identifiers to link biometric data to specific individuals, which can lead to the possibility of unauthorized linking of personal data across systems.

title: Identifier: Unique reference to identity of the data subject
description: The face authentication system employs unique identifiers that directly reference the identity of a data subject, which could enable tracing back to individuals without their consent.

title: Data type sensitivity: More sensitive data types collected than needed
description: The face authentication system collects sensitive biometric data, such as facial images, which may be more sensitive than what is necessary for the authentication process.

title: GDPR: Violating data minimization principle
description: The face authentication system may inadvertently violate the GDPR principle of data minimization by processing facial images that are not essential for the authentication process.

title: Linking based on identifier that is unique
description: The ML process may use unique identifiers that can link the data processed to identifiable individuals, creating a risk of linking personal data to individuals.

title: Identifier reveals identity of data subject
description: The ML process may rely on unique references to the identity of the data subjects, which can make their identification possible and compromise their anonymity.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: The ML feature extraction may handle sensitive data types that exceed the functional requirements of the system, thereby creating unnecessary risks of data exposure.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The data processed by the ML Model may result in collecting more personal data than is necessary for its intended functionality, violating GDPR principles.

title: Linking based on a unique identifier
description: The biometric data processed can serve as a unique identifier, enabling potential linking of identifiable individuals to specific data points within the biometric database.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes biometric data that is inherently identifiable due to its unique characteristics. This poses a risk of individual identification.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Biometric data is considered highly sensitive, and the collection for purposes beyond strict necessity introduces the risk of unauthorized access or misuse.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Data subjects may be unaware that their biometric information is being processed, leading to a lack of informed consent.

title: GDPR-related noncompliance due to insufficient data subject controls
description: The processing of biometric data may not comply with GDPR if there are insufficient controls for data subjects to manage their rights regarding consent and access.

title: Unique identifier risk in appropriateness check
description: The appropriateness check processes data that may contain unique identifiers, potentially linking the data to individuals. This linking could compromise user anonymity and privacy if unique identifiers are processed without adequate safeguards.

title: Identifier processing risk in appropriateness check
description: The appropriateness check might process data containing unique identifiers that directly relate to individuals. If mishandled or breached, this could lead to the identification of data subjects.

title: Sensitive data type collection risk in appropriateness check
description: If the appropriateness check collects more sensitive data types than functionally necessary, there’s a risk of unnecessary exposure and processing of personal data that could harm user privacy.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The appropriateness check may be processing more personal data than is necessary for its functional goals, violating data minimization principles as per GDPR.

title: Unnecessary data treatment in biometric comparison
description: The biometric comparison process may involve the treatment, analysis, or enrichment of personal data that is not necessary to achieve the functionality of the system, risking unnecessary data exposure.

title: Unique Identifier Risk
description: The system may link data back to the user through unique identifiers used in the face authentication process, potentially compromising their privacy.

title: Processing of Identified Data
description: The face authentication system processes identified data (facial features) which are directly linked to the user's identity, raising privacy concerns.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: The system collects sensitive biometric data types (facial recognition) which may not be strictly necessary for its functionality.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with GDPR
description: The processing of biometric data may lead to GDPR non-compliance if there is a lack of valid consent for data processing and insufficient controls for data subject rights.

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: The system may link the user to their unique identifier (e.g., user ID) during face authentication, potentially exposing personal information if the identifier is compromised.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The face authentication system processes identifiable information that can directly link back to the user, posing a risk of unauthorized identification.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: The face authentication process may collect sensitive biometric data that exceeds what is functionally required, raising privacy concerns.

title: GDPR-related noncompliance
description: The processing of face authentication data may violate GDPR principles, such as insufficient user consent for processing personal data.

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: Users may be unaware of the extent to which their personal data is being collected and processed by the face authentication system.
